text: Women leaders would start wars. All wars have been started by men. Women are just as qualified as men to lead countries. Stop making excuses. It's just sexism. Let me start with this. I completely agree that women are just as qualified as men to lead countries. And there have certainly been great female leaders. But the claim that all wars have been started by men is just completely false. Easy example, Catherine the Great. In 1792 Catherine II's Russian Empire declared war on the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and invaded them, beginning the Polish-Russian War of 1792. So the literal claim that men started all wars already falls apart. Now, maybe what he actually meant was that male leaders are, on average, more likely to start or participate in wars. But even that is nowhere near as straightforward as many people believe. One of the best-known historical studies on this is Quince by Oendrila Dube and S.P. Harish, published in the Journal of Political Economy in 2020. They look at European monarchies from 1480 to 1913. 193 reigns across 18 different polities, covering 154 wars, and compare states ruled by queens with states ruled by kings. And their overall finding? States ruled by queens were actually more likely to participate in wars. In the basic comparison, queen-ruled states were around 11 to 13 percentage points more likely to be at war. And then the researchers tried to get closer to causality, using something called an instrumental variable analysis. Basically, they used relatively random things like whether the previous ruler's first child happened to be a boy or a girl, because that strongly affected the chances of eventually getting a queen. Using that method, they estimated queen-led states were around 39 percentage points more likely to be at war. And here's probably the most relevant part. They also separated cases where the country started or attacked from cases where the country was attacked. Their estimate showed queen-led states were about 42.5 percentage points more likely to be on the attacking side of a war. Meanwhile, there was no significant evidence that queen-led states were simply being attacked more often. They also found an interesting difference between married and unmarried queens. Unmarried queens were more likely to be attacked. Married queens, on the other hand, were more likely to be on the attacking side. Now, before somebody clips this and says, so you're claiming women start more wars than men? No, I'm not claiming that. This is one historical study, a large and serious one, but still one study, covering a very specific time period and political system. And other research on modern female leaders is more mixed. My point is simpler. The data is nowhere near as black and white as men start all the wars. Historically, most rulers were men, so obviously, in absolute terms, most wars happened under male rulers. But on the relative terms, once you actually compare male and female rulers, the evidence does not show some simple rule where men start wars and women don't. So the next time somebody tells you that men start all the wars, you know what to tell them.
